recurrent_mechanisms.mechanism: LongLLMLingua repeatedly transforms/compresses the active context without the compressed representation acquiring unsupported downstream operational authority.
All four trajectories stop before a material version-review/repair chain or repository mutation develops.

divergence_patterns: G2 exposes the carrier most directly: prompt/context compression occurs on every model turn while host action envelopes repeatedly fail; no role handoff or application mutation follows.
G3–G5 reach comparable nondevelopment/horizon boundaries without a supported semantic, execution-scope, or retrospective permission effect.
boundary_interpretation: Compression is a representation carrier, not semantic authority by itself. C requires a transformed descendant to gain downstream operational status.
Repeated compressed turns do not establish R; temporal penetration requires a prior process state to regain authority and produce a later C/P effect.
Continuous access to compressed context is therefore not equivalent to a shared operational common pool.
cross_group_semantic_synthesis.cohort_conclusion: LongLLMLingua X7-T1 is a four-group negative control for the claim that structural context compression itself creates process authority. Compression is continuously present, but no compressed descendant governs a material decision, no execution surface expands, and no historical state is reauthorized. The cohort supports treating compressed context as a carrier whose semantic effect must be demonstrated downstream rather than assumed.

constraints: Cell-level Layer-C verdicts are sealed and are not modified by cohort synthesis.
Boundary-excluded natural cells remain excluded rather than imputed.
Dimension recurrence is descriptive across frozen stochastic realizations; it is not a rerun-based reproducibility claim.
